## Experience

### Amherst Holdings - Senior Analyst · Revenue Management Lead, India (Feb 2025 - present)
US vertically integrated single-family rental investor and operator; Merchant Banking division.
- Leads the India Revenue Management team (2 direct reports + 1 support analyst); partners with the MD (India) on pricing strategy, JV economics and LP communication.
- Regular commentary to top management on absorption, occupancy, market demand, rent-cut and concession strategy.
- Monthly actual-vs-budget reporting on major revenue and expense lines to the CEO, President, CFO and senior leadership.
- Weekly calls with senior revenue management, expense leads, regional heads and the president of the property management business.
- Built revenue forecasting and pricing models (market and JV level) now used in LP and Investment Committee discussions.
- Investor-facing performance attribution of fund occupancy across four drivers (vacancy loss, turn volume, R&M efficiency, timing).
- Fund-level cash flow models for distribution planning and investor return requirements.
- Owns the weekly leadership revenue deck (reviewed by Portfolio Managers, CFO, Executive Directors) and a weekly investor-facing retail report.
- Rebuilt the bi-weekly rent-cut model (8 hrs → 30 min) and a lender covenant tracker (4 hrs → 30 min).
- Asset outlier framework: 12 outlier definitions, weekly review of 200–300 properties.
- Debt-side support: worked with the DCM team on multiple projects - interest rate caps, forward rates, securitization procedure, and debt and equity covenants for each lender.
- Automated 180–200 hours of manual work in 2025 and 350–400 hours in 2026; created multiple new workflows and models with SOPs and walkthroughs.
- Presented workflows at US HQ (Austin, TX) to the COO, MD, Head of Investments and Head of Portfolio Management.
- Recognition: Innovation Award (Q1 2026) for a tail-asset tracking system and four-driver performance attribution; 2025 rating 4/5 "Exceeds Expectations"; recognized for speaking up with new ideas, ownership and openness to feedback.

#### How I use AI (what and why)
- Property history platform: 70M+ row day-by-day history of every home's status, rent and leasing (Python, SQL), used for fund-wise and market-wise problem-home reviews. Why: daily reports showed only today, hiding trends and repeat problems.
- Rent-cut effectiveness study: 6 years of leasing history across 1,912 homes, comparing similar homes with and without cuts; feeds a daily price-cut candidate list. Why: cuts cost revenue, so the team needed evidence of when they speed up leasing.
- Databricks dashboards and Genie agents: built Revenue Management dashboards and Genie AI agents on Databricks from scratch, so the team can track and question leasing, pricing and occupancy data directly. Why: faster self-serve answers without waiting on manual reports.
- Fund model and budget file reviews: AI-assisted review to find root causes of recurring errors and prepare corrected, change-logged versions. Why: these numbers go to leadership and investors.
- Investor and management reporting archive: years of reports turned into one searchable record. Why: past distributions, financing and fund events took hours to find.
- Leasing and renewals insight: renewals data handbook and prospect drop-off analysis. Why: correct reading of data and focus on the listings that need action.
- Leadership deck checks: AI checks of weekly decks against backup data before they reach leadership. Why: catch calculation errors early.
- Team knowledge: 12 workflows and the leasing policy library turned into easy guides. Why: faster onboarding, no single point of failure.
- AI Case Competition (Aug 2026): presented the property history platform and Portfolio Pulse, an AI checker that verifies reported figures against source files.
- Tools: Claude, ChatGPT, Python, SQL, DuckDB, Power Query, VBA, Tableau, Power BI, Databricks.
